definition: The Mivar-based approach is a mathematical tool for designing artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
details: Mivar (Multidimensional Informational Variable Adaptive Reality) was developed by combining production and Petri nets. The Mivar-based approach was developed for semantic analysis and adequate representation of humanitarian epistemological and axiological principles in the process of developing artificial intelligence. The Mivar-based approach incorporates computer science, informatics and discrete mathematics, databases, expert systems, graph theory, matrices and inference systems. The Mivar-based approach involves two technologies: Information accumulation is a method of creating global evolutionary data-and-rules bases with variable structure. It works on the basis of adaptive, discrete, mivar-oriented information space, unified data and rules representation, based on three main concepts: "object, property, relation". Information accumulation is designed to store any information with possible evolutionary structure and without limitations concerning the amount of information and forms of its presentation. explainer.lead: The Mivar-based approach is a mathematical tool for designing AI systems, built on Multidimensional Informational Variable Adaptive Reality (Mivar) models. It matters as a formal framework for representing knowledge and inference in expert systems.

tiers.eli5: It is a way of drawing up the rules of a problem as a network so a computer can reason through them.
tiers.practitioner: Designers use it for semantic analysis and for representing knowledge in expert systems. A pitfall is its breadth: it pulls together computer science, discrete mathematics, databases, graph theory, matrices and inference systems, so applying it demands familiarity with several fields.
tiers.paperLevel: Mivar combines production systems and Petri nets; the approach draws on computer science, informatics, discrete mathematics, databases, expert systems, graph theory, matrices and inference systems, and was developed to represent humanitarian epistemological and axiological principles in AI development.

explainer.example: A designer could encode a domain's facts and rules as a Mivar graph and run inference over it to answer queries.
